forecasts.reason: GPU compute dominates; graphs remove only ~3-5% of launch overhead, the gain sits right at the 3% threshold, and integrating Muon/Lookahead risks leaks.
Muon renormalizes filters, so weight decay only touches BN biases, whitening bias and head; expect noise, not +0.3 pp.
Few real host syncs and compute-bound steps mean a cut of about 1-2%, under 3%; folding augmentation in likely changes the RNG stream, so results are not bit-identical.
Lookahead's fast-weight resets probably carry part of the value; a plain short-horizon EMA likely loses 0.1-0.4 pp, straddling the 0.3 pp threshold and likely dropping below the bar.

cruxes: What is E010's mean on held-out seeds 3-12? If it is below 0.753, every time-saving idea must first buy back margin (about 2 s/pp via epochs).
What fraction of a 26 ms step is GPU idle under the 4-CPU pin? This decides whether CUDA graphs and graph-break removal can save more than 3%.
Is there any accuracy lever cheaper than about 2 s/pp (BN-stat recompute, a longer 32 px tail with a shorter 24 px head) that could fund further resolution or width cuts?
